verses.text: Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the strangers scattered throughout Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia, and Bithynia,

Elect (chosen) according to the foreknowledge (knowing ahead of time) of God the Father, through sanctification (being made holy) of the Spirit, to obedience and sprinkling of the blood of Jesus Christ: Grace to you, and peace, be multiplied.

Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ. By His great mercy God has begotten us again (given us new birth) to a lively (living) hope, by the resurrection (rising) of Jesus Christ from the dead,
To an inheritance incorruptible (that never decays), and undefiled (pure), and that does not fade away, reserved (kept) in heaven for you.
You are kept by the power of God through faith to salvation, ready to be revealed (shown) in the last time.
In this you greatly rejoice, though now for a season (short time), if need be, you are in heaviness (sorrow) through manifold (many kinds of) temptations (trials).

This is so that the trial (testing) of your faith, being much more precious than gold that perishes, though it is tried (tested) with fire, might be found to praise and honor and glory at the appearing of Jesus Christ.
You love Jesus Christ, though you have not seen Him. Though now you do not see Him, yet believing, you rejoice with joy unspeakable (too great to tell) and full of glory.
You are receiving the end (goal) of your faith, even the salvation of your souls.
About this salvation the prophets have enquired (asked) and searched diligently (carefully). They prophesied (spoke God's message) of the grace that would come to you.

They searched what time, or what kind of time, the Spirit of Christ which was in them did signify (point to). The Spirit testified (told) beforehand the sufferings of Christ, and the glory that would follow.

It was revealed (shown) to the prophets that they were serving not themselves, but us, in the things which are now reported to you. These things were told to you by those who have preached the gospel (good news) to you with the Holy Spirit sent down from heaven. The angels desire to look into these things.
So gird up the loins of your mind (get your mind ready). Be sober (clear minded). And hope to the end for the grace that is to be brought to you at the revelation (showing) of Jesus Christ.
As obedient children, do not fashion (shape) yourselves according to the former lusts (wrong desires) you had in your ignorance (not knowing).
But as the One who has called you is holy, so you be holy in all manner of conversation (way of life).
Because it is written: Be holy, for I am holy.

And if you call on the Father, who without respect of persons (treating some better than others) judges according to every man's work, pass the time of your sojourning (stay as strangers) here in fear.

For you know that you were not redeemed (bought back and set free) with corruptible (decaying) things, like silver and gold, from your vain (empty) conversation (way of life) received by tradition from your fathers.
But you were redeemed (bought back and set free) with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish (flaw) and without spot.
Christ truly was foreordained (chosen ahead of time) before the foundation of the world. But He was manifest (shown clearly) in these last times for you.
By Christ you believe in God, who raised Christ up from the dead, and gave Him glory, so that your faith and hope might be in God.

Seeing you have purified (made pure) your souls in obeying the truth through the Spirit to unfeigned (not pretended) love of the brothers, see that you love one another with a pure heart fervently (deeply).
You are born again, not of corruptible (decaying) seed, but of incorruptible (never decaying) seed, by the word of God, which lives and abides (lasts) forever.
For all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as the flower of grass. The grass withers, and its flower falls away.
But the word of the Lord endures (lasts) forever. And this is the word which by the gospel (good news) is preached to you.

verses.text: So laying aside all malice (hate), and all guile (tricks), and hypocrisies (pretending), and envies (jealousy), and all evil speakings,
As newborn babes (babies), desire the sincere (pure) milk of the word, so that you may grow by it.
If so be you have tasted that the Lord is gracious (kind).
You come to Him, as to a living stone, disallowed (rejected) indeed by men, but chosen by God, and precious.
You also, as lively (living) stones, are built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood. You offer up spiritual sacrifices, acceptable to God by Jesus Christ.

So also it is contained in the Scripture: Look, I lay in Sion (Zion) a chief corner stone (the most important stone), elect (chosen), precious. And the one who believes on Him will not be confounded (put to shame).
So to you who believe He is precious. But to those who are disobedient, the stone which the builders disallowed (rejected), the same is made the head of the corner (the most important stone).
And He is a stone of stumbling, and a rock of offence, even to those who stumble at the word, being disobedient. To this also they were appointed.

But you are a chosen generation (people), a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a peculiar (special, owned by God) people. This is so that you should show forth the praises of the One who has called you out of darkness into His marvellous light.
In time past you were not a people, but now you are the people of God. You had not obtained mercy, but now you have obtained mercy.
Dearly beloved (dear friends), I beg you as strangers and pilgrims (travelers): abstain (stay away) from fleshly lusts (wrong desires of the body), which war against the soul.

Have your conversation (way of life) honest among the Gentiles (people who are not Jews). Then, though they speak against you as evildoers, they may by your good works, which they will see, glorify God in the day of visitation (when God comes).
Submit yourselves to every ordinance (law) of man for the Lord's sake, whether it is to the king, as supreme (highest),
Or to governors, as to those who are sent by him for the punishment of evildoers, and for the praise of those who do well.
For this is the will of God, that by doing well you may put to silence the ignorance (not knowing) of foolish men.
Live as free, and do not use your liberty (freedom) for a cloke (cover) of maliciousness (evil), but live as the servants of God.
Honor all men. Love the brotherhood (fellow believers). Fear God. Honor the king.
Servants, be subject to your masters with all fear, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the froward (harsh).
For this is thankworthy (pleasing to God), if a man, for conscience toward God, endures grief, suffering wrongfully.
For what glory is it, if, when you are buffeted (beaten) for your faults, you take it patiently? But if, when you do well and suffer for it, you take it patiently, this is acceptable with God.
For even to this you were called. Because Christ also suffered for us, leaving us an example, that you should follow His steps.
Christ did no sin, and no guile (lie) was found in His mouth.
When Christ was reviled (insulted), He did not revile (insult) back. When He suffered, He did not threaten. But He committed (gave) Himself to God who judges righteously (fairly).
Christ His own self bore our sins in His own body on the tree (cross). This is so that we, being dead to sins, should live to righteousness (what is right). By His stripes (wounds) you were healed.
For you were like sheep going astray (wandering away). But now you have returned to the Shepherd and Bishop (Overseer) of your souls.

verses.text: In the same way, you wives, be in subjection (submit) to your own husbands. Then, if any husbands do not obey the word, they also may be won without the word by the conversation (way of life) of the wives.
The husbands will see your chaste (pure) conversation (way of life) joined with fear.
Let your adorning (beauty) not be that outward adorning of plaiting (braiding) the hair, and of wearing of gold, or of putting on of clothes.

But let it be the hidden man of the heart (the inner self), in what is not corruptible (does not decay), even the ornament (beauty) of a meek (gentle) and quiet spirit. This is of great price in the sight of God.
For in this way in the old time the holy women also, who trusted in God, adorned (made beautiful) themselves. They were in subjection (submitted) to their own husbands.
Even as Sara (Sarah) obeyed Abraham, calling him lord. You are her daughters, as long as you do well, and are not afraid with any amazement (fear).

In the same way, you husbands, dwell (live) with your wives according to knowledge (understanding). Give honor to the wife, as to the weaker vessel, and as being heirs together of the grace of life. Then your prayers will not be hindered (blocked).
Finally, all of you be of one mind. Have compassion one for another. Love as brothers. Be pitiful (tender hearted). Be courteous (kind).
Do not render (give back) evil for evil, or railing (insult) for railing (insult). But instead give blessing, knowing that you are called to this, so that you should inherit a blessing.
For whoever wants to love life, and see good days, let them refrain (keep) their tongue from evil, and their lips so that they speak no guile (lies).
Let them eschew (turn away from) evil, and do good. Let them seek peace, and ensue (go after) it.
For the eyes of the Lord are over the righteous (those who are right with God), and His ears are open to their prayers. But the face of the Lord is against those who do evil.
And who is he that will harm you, if you are followers of what is good?
But if you suffer for righteousness' sake (doing what is right), happy are you. And do not be afraid of their terror, and do not be troubled.
But sanctify (set apart as holy) the Lord God in your hearts. And be ready always to give an answer to every man who asks you a reason of the hope that is in you, with meekness (gentleness) and fear.
Have a good conscience. Then, while they speak evil of you as of evildoers, they may be ashamed who falsely accuse your good conversation (way of life) in Christ.
For it is better, if the will of God is so, that you suffer for well doing, than for evil doing.

For Christ also has once suffered for sins, the just (right) for the unjust (wrong), so that He might bring us to God. He was put to death in the flesh (body), but quickened (made alive) by the Spirit.
By the Spirit also Christ went and preached to the spirits in prison,

Who in the past were disobedient, when once the longsuffering (patience) of God waited in the days of Noah, while the ark (big boat) was being prepared. In the ark few, that is, eight souls, were saved by water.

The like figure (picture) to this, baptism, does also now save us. Not the putting away of the filth (dirt) of the flesh (body), but the answer of a good conscience toward God, by the resurrection (rising) of Jesus Christ.
Jesus Christ has gone into heaven, and is on the right hand of God. Angels and authorities and powers are made subject to Him.

verses.text: So since Christ has suffered for us in the flesh (body), arm yourselves likewise with the same mind. For the one who has suffered in the flesh (body) has ceased (stopped) from sin.
So that believer should no longer live the rest of his time in the flesh (body) for the lusts (wrong desires) of men, but for the will of God.

For the time past of our life may suffice (be enough) for us to have done the will of the Gentiles (people who are not Jews). We walked in lasciviousness (wild sinful living), lusts (wrong desires), excess of wine, revellings (wild parties), banquetings (drunken feasts), and abominable (disgusting) idolatries (worship of idols).
In this they think it strange that you do not run with them to the same excess of riot (wild living). So they speak evil of you.
They will give account to the One who is ready to judge the living and the dead.
For this reason the gospel (good news) was preached also to those who are dead. This was so that they might be judged according to men in the flesh (body), but live according to God in the spirit.
But the end of all things is at hand (near). So be sober (clear minded), and watch (stay alert) to prayer.
And above all things have fervent (deep) charity (love) among yourselves. For charity (love) will cover the multitude (great number) of sins.
Use hospitality (welcoming strangers) one to another without grudging (complaining).
As every man has received the gift, even so minister (serve) the same one to another, as good stewards (managers) of the manifold (many kinds of) grace of God.

If any man speaks, let him speak as the oracles (words) of God. If any man ministers (serves), let him do it as of the ability which God gives. Then God in all things may be glorified through Jesus Christ. To Him be praise and dominion (power) forever and ever. Amen.
Beloved (dear friends), do not think it strange about the fiery trial which is to try (test) you, as though some strange thing happened to you.
But rejoice, because you are partakers (sharers) of Christ's sufferings. Then, when His glory is revealed (shown), you may be glad also with exceeding (great) joy.
If you are reproached (insulted) for the name of Christ, happy are you. For the Spirit of glory and of God rests on you. On their part Christ is evil spoken of, but on your part He is glorified.
But let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or as an evildoer, or as a busybody in other men's matters.
Yet if any man suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed. But let him glorify God on this behalf.
For the time has come that judgment must begin at the house of God. And if it first begins at us, what will the end be of those who do not obey the gospel (good news) of God?
And if the righteous (those who are right with God) are scarcely (hardly) saved, where will the ungodly and the sinner appear?
So let those who suffer according to the will of God commit (give) the keeping of their souls to God in well doing, as to a faithful Creator.

verses.text: The elders who are among you I exhort (encourage). I am also an elder, and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and also a partaker (sharer) of the glory that will be revealed (shown).

Feed the flock of God which is among you, taking the oversight (care) of it. Do it not by constraint (because you must), but willingly. Do it not for filthy lucre (dishonest money), but of a ready mind.
Do not be lords over God's heritage (people), but be examples to the flock.
And when the chief Shepherd appears, you will receive a crown of glory that does not fade away.

In the same way, you younger, submit yourselves to the elder. Yes, all of you be subject one to another, and be clothed with humility. For God resists (stands against) the proud, and gives grace to the humble.
So humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, so that God may exalt (lift up) you in due time.
Cast all your care on God, for God cares for you.
Be sober (clear minded). Be vigilant (watchful). Because your adversary (enemy) the devil, as a roaring lion, walks about, seeking whom he may devour (eat up).
Resist (stand against) the devil, stedfast (firm) in the faith. Know that the same afflictions (troubles) are accomplished (happening) in your brothers who are in the world.
But may the God of all grace, who has called us to His eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a while, make you perfect (complete), stablish (make firm), strengthen, and settle you.
To Him be glory and dominion (power) forever and ever. Amen.
By Silas, a faithful brother to you, as I suppose, I have written briefly. I am exhorting (encouraging) you, and testifying (telling) that this is the true grace of God in which you stand.
The church that is at Babylon, elected (chosen) together with you, salutes (greets) you. And so does Mark my son.
Greet one another with a kiss of charity (love). Peace be with you all who are in Christ Jesus. Amen.
